todays_goal: Complete the camera-image lesson missed on Day 16.

lessons.subject: science
lessons.previous_learning: Lens/refraction concepts were developed on Day 15. Day 16 camera lesson was not completed.
lessons.course_context: Apply the lens model to a camera and compare pinhole versus lens imaging.
learning_objectives: Explain how light from a scene reaches a sensor.
lessons.why_it_matters: The same light-path ideas explain cameras, eyes, microscopes, and other imaging technology.

vocabulary.definition: the light-detecting surface in a digital camera
when rays land in positions that make the image sharp
a very small opening that limits the rays entering a camera

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: light from the scene enters the camera. A lens bends the rays so they land in an organized pattern on the sensor. A pinhole can form an image without a lens, but it lets in much less light.

worked_examples.title: Pinhole camera
worked_examples.problem: Why can a tiny hole form an image?
worked_examples.solution: It limits which rays from each scene point reach the screen.
worked_examples.explanation: The paths stay organized, but little light enters.

worked_examples.title: Lens camera
worked_examples.solution: It gathers more light and bends rays toward useful places on the sensor.
worked_examples.explanation: This can create a brighter focused image.

independent_practice.prompt: What does the lens do to light?
Why is a pinhole image dim?
What does focused mean in a camera?
Draw object -> lens -> sensor and show rays changing direction.

exit_ticket.prompt: Why can a camera form an image without the object touching the camera?
exit_ticket.answer: Light carries information from the object into the camera.

exit_ticket.prompt: Explain one difference between a pinhole camera and a lens camera.
exit_ticket.answer: A pinhole camera lets in very little light; a lens camera collects more light and refracts it to form a brighter focused image.

lessons.voice_prompt: Teach first. Use the whiteboard to draw OBJECT -> LENS -> SENSOR and a different example of top/bottom rays. Ask short questions. Do not draw Atticus's assigned final diagram.
